name: AD — Kerberos Replay Attack Detected
description: Windows event 4649 is logged when the Kerberos subsystem detects a replayed authenticator — the same request submitted twice. It is a direct indicator of ticket replay, pass-the-ticket and relay tooling, and it is one of the few Windows events that is almost never produced by normal operation. Validated baseline at JCB: 5 events across 7 days on a single host. No existing rule covers this event code.
author: ScanWave
note:
### Triage
1. Establish the account and host in the event, then review all Kerberos activity (4768/4769/4771) for that account around the same time.
2. A cluster of 4649 events, or 4649 on a domain controller or Tier-0 server, should be treated as active credential-material abuse.
3. Correlate with `Windows — Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash Logon Pattern`, `AD — Kerberoasting: RC4 Service Ticket Requested` and `AD — DCSync: Directory Replication by an Unexpected Principal`.
4. Isolated single events can result from network retransmission — investigate but weigh volume and destination.
false_positives: Network-level packet duplication or an aggressive load balancer replaying authentication traffic.
Misbehaving application that caches and resubmits a Kerberos authenticator.
